item.title: D2 BOYS WRESTLING: Mid Valley’s Youngblood leads strong outing from No. 6 seeds

item.title: D2 BOYS BASKETBALL: League powers to clash in semifinal rounds
item.description: Lackawanna League teams powered their way into the District 2 boys basketball semifinals last week, setting up a much-anticipated exciting Saturday afternoon. item.title: HS FIELD HOCKEY: Wallenpaupack’s Ey named to U16 United States National Team
item.description: Emma Ey is committed to working toward a dream in a sport she loves. In January, the Wallenpaupack freshman and Times-Tribune All-Region field hockey player was selected to the U-16 United States Women’s National Team. Since then, Ey has worked with the top players in the country at her level while also continuing to develop her skills. item.title: Adopt a Boxer Rescue accepts donation from the Cawley family
item.description: Stacy and Brett Cawley presented Adopt a Boxer Rescue with a check in honor of their beloved son, Michael “Chippi” Cawley. Funds were raised at the Michael “Chippi” Cawley One Last Cast third annual race. First row, from left: Stacy Cawley, Maple Rowlands, boxers Kaia and River, and Brett Cawley. Second row: Jen Radzwillowicz; Pamela Rowlands, secretary; Dawn Karem, president, AaBR; Gayle Devine and Beth Boylan.

item.title: Easter Egg Hunt scheduled
item.description: Easter Egg Hunt committee members of the Dunmore Lions Club, Dunmore Rotary, Dunmore Police Department and Dunmore Fire Department met recently for the upcoming Easter Egg Hunt, scheduled for Saturday, April 4, at 10 a.m. at St. Anthony’s Playground, Hill and Cooney streets, for ages 11 and younger. item.title: D2 GIRLS BASKETBALL: Mountain View rallies past Holy Cross to reach 2A final
item.description: KINGSLEY — Holy Cross’ torrid 3-point shooting enabled it to build a nine-point lead early in the third quarter of its District 2 Class 2A girls basketball semifinal, forcing Mountain View coach Corey Gesford to call timeout. His message to his team in the huddle: Relax. We’ve been here before. The Lady Eagles did just that.
